facts: Bathocyroe fosteri is a species of lobate ctenophore found at intermediate depths in all the world's oceans.
The species is very common and abundant near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
It is bioluminescent, and is typically observed hanging motionlessly in an upright or inverted posture although it can flap its oral lobes to swim.

panels.desc: A medium shot of the transparent, bioluminescent ctenophore figurine hanging upside down in a dark, deep-sea setting made of crumpled blue cellophane. It is suspended by barely visible fine threads. The upper quarter of the frame is dark and uncluttered for captions. Shallow depth of field blurs the background.

A close-up shot focusing on the two large, prominent oral lobes of the ctenophore figurine. Tiny LED fairy lights illuminate its transparent, deeply cleft bell-like body, revealing the red-pigmented inner gut. Small bits of cotton-wool marine snow float around it on fine wires. The upper quarter remains calm and dark.

A wide shot showing the edge of a wooden worktable. On the table, a miniature diorama features the ctenophore figurine suspended in a clear resin block, next to a tiny clay scientist figurine looking at it. Behind them is a painted cardboard backdrop of a world map. The warm glow of a desk lamp illuminates the scene. The upper quarter is an uncluttered painted wall.

A wide shot inside an open cardboard display box, with the corrugated edge visible on the side. The ctenophore figurine is posed dynamically with its oral lobes flared outwards as if flapping to swim. It moves past paper-cut deep-sea rocks, suspended by thin bent wires. The upper quarter is calm and softly lit.

A wide shot showing a green cutting mat at the bottom edge of the frame. Above it, a miniature deep-sea diorama features the ctenophore figurine hanging completely motionless, upside down. A tiny, hand-painted toy ROV submarine made of clay and wire hovers nearby, shining a tiny LED beam onto the creature. The upper quarter is a smooth, uncluttered dark backdrop.

A dynamic, striking wide shot from a slightly high angle. The ctenophore figurine's large oral lobes are spread wide open like a parachute, engulfing a tiny, brightly painted clay copepod prey. The scene is dramatized with warm, directional miniature spotlighting, with cotton-wool marine snow blurring in the strong tilt-shift depth of field. The upper quarter is left dark and clear.

A close-up shot focused on the inner structure of the ctenophore. Fine, thread-like tentacles are wrapped around the tiny clay prey, pulling it upwards into the central gut structure, which is vividly painted with red satin paint. The transparent body catches the warm light. The upper quarter is softly blurred and empty.

A wide shot showing the edge of a warm desk lamp hood at the top right corner, leaving the rest of the upper area calm and dark. The ctenophore figurine hangs upside down, its bioluminescence very dim, receding into the deep shadows of a black painted cardboard backdrop. Small bits of felt marine snow hang motionless in the fading light.

어두운 바다 속, 거꾸로 된 자세로 가만히 매달려 있는 투명한 생물입니다. 2~4cm 크기의 구강 엽을 넓게 펼쳐 다가오는 먹이를 가둡니다. 그리고 붙잡은 먹이를 촉수를 이용해 붉은색 내장 안으로 끌어들입니다. 평소에는 움직이지 않으며, 먹이를 삼킨 후에도 다시 조용히 바다를 떠다닙니다.
